claims.text: Replacing classical EAM references with a machine-learning potential will improve reference–target phase-space overlap.
Replacing classical EAM references with a machine-learning potential will substantially reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
The proposed machine-learning potential is trained on ab initio data covering solid and liquid configurations near high melting temperatures.
The intervention applies to complex multielement high-entropy alloys near or above their melting points.
The intervention also applies to analogous elemental and binary systems under similar thermal conditions.
The machine-learning potential serves as a surrogate energy model between the reference and ab initio target systems.
The machine-learning potential will capture many-body interactions more effectively than traditional EAM models.
The machine-learning potential will capture the full spectrum of atomic configurations sampled by the relevant phases.
Capturing many-body interactions and a broader spectrum of configurations will improve phase-space overlap.
Improved phase-space overlap will produce a smoother thermodynamic-integration path than an EAM reference.
The integration-path mismatch may decrease by approximately a factor of two or more.
The machine-learning reference will yield free-energy calculations closer to fully ab initio results than the EAM reference.
TOR-TILD EAM reference potentials insufficiently represent the configurational diversity of the ab initio liquid.
The insufficient configurational representation of TOR-TILD EAM references causes larger thermodynamic-integration path mismatches.
The benefit of the machine-learning potential may be less pronounced in near-pure elemental systems, highly ordered intermetallics, or systems far below melting.
The magnitude of mismatch reduction depends on the quality and extent of the ab initio training data.
Elemental and binary calculations provide evidence that machine-learning potentials improve phase-space overlap.
Transferability of the proposed improvement to complex multicomponent alloys has not been fully validated.
